title: When the Cellar Turns
premise: Xanthe Coldharbour takes a teaching post at Marrowfen Academy, where a class vanished decades ago and the cellar door is counted twice nightly. When every mirror begins lagging one second behind reality, Xanthe realizes the missing students never left — they were sung into the house's reflection, and the school's founding families have fed it ever since to keep their power. To free them, Xanthe must learn the song's final verse from the trapped children themselves without joining the chorus, while falling for Wren, the caretaker whose family built the trap. In the end, Xanthe sings the verse alone in the dark, shattering the mirrors and the town's complicity, and chooses love and outlaw justice over the duty of silence.
about_author: Ada Zhou is the pen name of a former night-shift teacher who swears her old school had one more staircase than the blueprints showed. She writes horror about institutions that eat people politely.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Twice
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Arriving at Marrowfen Academy, Xanthe learns the rules: lights on, doors counted, cellar locked at dusk. The headmaster's warmth feels rehearsed; caretaker Wren watches Xanthe with pity. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging — Xanthe wants this fresh start too badly to question it.

chapters.title: The Missing Roster
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Teaching a half-empty class, Xanthe finds a 1974 register with eleven names struck through in red. Asking around earns polite deflections and one warning note: STOP COUNTING. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the town closes ranks.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In the staff bathroom mirror, Xanthe's reflection moves a beat behind. By nightfall every mirror in the boarding house lags exactly one second. Wren admits they've seen it before — the year their sister disappeared. Beat: isolation breaks; an alliance forms.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren reveals the founding families' bargain: the school sings children into its reflection to preserve the town's fortune. Wren has spent years pretending not to know. Beat: guilt and complicity — love beginning against loyalty to blood.

chapters.title: The Verse Without Words
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Following humming through the walls, Xanthe finds the sealed music room where sheet music shows only the first two verses. The third page is blank — or written in something that only appears in reflections. Beat: hunger for forbidden knowledge.

chapters.title: Chorus of the Kept
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Pulled through a lagging mirror into the reflected school, Xanthe meets the eleven students, unaged, still rehearsing a song that keeps them docile. They beg her not to sing along. Beat: heartbreak — the missing class was never missing, only kept.

chapters.title: The Families Assemble
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The founding families discover Xanthe's snooping and stage a 'welcome dinner' that is really a warning, with the headmaster reciting the school's history like scripture. Wren must choose between exposing Xanthe and lying to kin. Beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Learning by Heart
chapters.summary: POV alternating. In stolen nights, the trapped students teach Xanthe the last verse — which can only be learned, never written, and only by someone who refuses to join the chorus. Wren smuggles them candles and salt. Beat: tender defiance; love declared in whispers between verses.

chapters.title: When the Cellar Turns
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The equinox concert arrives; the families intend to add new names. Xanthe descends into the cellar as the house turns inside out, mirrors opening like doors, and begins singing the final verse alone while the chorus tries to swallow her voice. Beat: terror and resolve fused — the climax.

chapters.title: Counted Out
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The mirrors shatter; the eleven walk out aged to their proper years, and the town's fortune rots overnight. The families face the law they long outranked, and Wren testifies against them. Xanthe stays — not for the school, but for what they chose together. Beat: grief, justice, and hard-won love.
